key_insight: A six-dimensional adiabatic spectral submanifold (aSSM) model enables soft-robot reinforcement learning in 3 hours, versus an extrapolated 3 years of hardware interaction.
engineering_relevance: Compact, data-learned dynamics can accelerate controller training while enabling deployment on nonlinear soft hardware without policy fine-tuning.
method: Exploit time-scale separation to reduce soft-robot dynamics to an aSSM.
Learn a 6,924-parameter polynomial ordinary differential equation from pre-collected data.
Train a trajectory-tracking policy in the reduced simulator and deploy it directly.
evidence_signal: On a pneumatic soft arm, the policy achieved 40% lower dynamic-target tracking error than otherwise identical policies trained on RNN or transformer models; model identification took 5 minutes versus 13 and 100 hours, respectively.
watch_item: The abstract reports one soft-arm platform; transfer to other robots or operating regimes may require new data and validation of the time-scale separation.
paper_title: Accelerated Reinforcement Learning for Soft Robotics: Hours Instead of Years
